content.title: A24's ‘The Drama’ Plot Twist Spoilers And Ending, Explained
content.text: Robert Pattinson and Zendaya in "The Drama."A24Warning: Major spoilers ahead for The Drama.Writer-director Kristoffer Borgli’s new movie The Drama begs the question: Can a couple still genuinely love each other unconditionally after they’ve revealed the darkest, ugliest secrets about themselves? The film, now playing in theaters, stars Zendaya as Emma Harwood, a literary editor, and Robert Pattinson as Charlie Thompson, head curator at the Cambridge Art Museum. Days before their wedding, their blissful relationship is tested after a drunken game prompts Emma to reveal a shocking secret from her past. Although the press tour has presented the film as a rom-com, with Zendaya and Pattinson doing a skillful job at reinforcing that narrative, it’s more accurate to describe The Drama as a dark comedy that will likely make audiences squirm, wince and laugh as Emma and Charlie’s relationship unravels. Here’s a breakdown of the big plot twist in The Drama and what happens between Emma and Charlie. Zendaya’s Character, Emma, Almost Committed A Mass Shooting When She Was 15 Zendaya and Robert Pattinson in "The Drama."A24The movie’s big twist, which has been teased in the lead-up to the film’s release (and was leaked on Reddit), happens relatively early on. While tasting and finalizing the wedding reception menu with their friends Nate (Mamoudou Athie), the best man, and Rachel (Alana Haim), the maid of honor, Charlie and Emma mention that they spotted the DJ for the wedding smoking heroin on the street. This leads to a conversation about the ethics of still employing the DJ for the wedding, knowing that she’s a drug user. At Rachel’s suggestion, the group agrees to share the worst thing they’ve ever done. Nate used his ex-girlfriend as a human shield to protect himself from a vicious dog on a vacation, and Rachel locked a neighborhood kid, whom she called weird and autistic, in a closet of an RV overnight. The most scathing thing Charlie ever did was cyberbully a classmate so hard that the kid cried and his entire family moved. When Emma’s turn arrives, she takes a gulp of her wine and says, “I like, almost did a mass shooting.” Naturally, the vibe in the room shifts. Emma, now 30, explains that she was 15 and depressed, and took her dad’s rifle to school, intending to carry out a shooting. Emma also reveals that she’s deaf in her right ear because she positioned the gun too close to her ear while practicing her shooting in the woods, causing her eardrum to rupture. Zendaya in "The Drama."A24The following day, Charlie questions Emma about the almost-incident, which she wouldn’t have revealed if she hadn’t been so drunk the night before. Emma says that she moved around as a kid (her dad worked in the military) and when her family relocated to Louisiana, she found it hard to fit in or make friends and was bullied at school. She says that she was an angry child and was intrigued by the aesthetics of shootings and thought it looked cool, based on what she saw online. The Drama also includes flashbacks of young Emma (Jordyn Curet) styling her hair in braids, wearing dark eye makeup, and slinging a rifle across her body while standing in front of her computer’s webcam, trying to lean into the perceived cool aesthetic. Emma says that she got close to going through with her plan, but stopped herself after a shooting occurred at a mall in her area and three people died, including a classmate. She didn’t want to commit a shooting because someone else beat her to it. In the aftermath of the mall shooting, Emma joined an activist group at school, tossed her dad’s rifle in the river and started rallying for gun control. When Charlie asks if Emma felt like a fraud, she says it was more like waking up from a bad dream. Emma And Charlie Choose To Stay Together Robert Pattinson and Zendaya in "The Drama."A24The engaged couple agrees to go through with the wedding, but the longer Charlie fixates on Emma’s disturbing revelation, the more tainted his feelings for her become. Charlie slowly spirals and eventually asks his colleague, Misha (Hailey Benton Gates), what she’d do if her boyfriend, Blake (Michael Abbott Jr.), had almost committed a shooting. After talking with Misha, Charlie has a breakdown in his office. Misha tries to comfort him, but Charlie gets carried away and impulsively kisses her. They almost have sex, but Charlie stops himself. Charlie and Emma’s wedding ceremony goes off without a hitch, but the reception devolves into chaos. Emma’s dad gives a speech in which he recalls Emma developing a passion for gun control and becoming an activist in high school, which prompts Rachel to burst into laughter at the hypocrisy. Rachel, who distanced herself from Emma after her confession, doesn’t fully go off on Emma in her maid of honor speech, but gets in some digs about Emma being “layered” and “full of surprises.” Zendaya in "The Drama."A24While in the bathroom trying to compose herself, Emma overhears Misha telling someone about a shooting. Emma pulls Misha into a room with her and Charlie to find out if Rachel spilled her secret. But Mischa mistakenly assumes Emma wants to talk about Charlie kissing her at work, and blurts out the transgression.They all return to the reception and Charlie stumbles through his speech, trying to remember what he previously wrote before he found out Emma’s secret. He asks the whispering guests to stop gossiping, admits that he had a momentary lapse of judgment with Misha and says that he wouldn’t care if Emma did kill someone. As he grows more frustrated, Charlie snaps at Blake and tells him to shut up. Blake rushes Charlie and beats him up, and Charlie returns to his apartment bloody and bruised. Emma, meanwhile, leaves with her parents and ignores Charlie’s calls and messages. While still in his bloody groomswear, Charlie goes to a nearby diner to eat. Emma walks in and joins him at his table, and Charlie becomes emotional, telling her he’s sorry. She pretends they’re strangers and asks his name and if he lives around here. She also asks Charlie about his bruised face, and he makes up a story about trying to save a woman from being robbed. She becomes teary and they shake hands across the table. “It’s nice to meet you, Emma,” Charlie says. The movie ends with Charlie and Emma smiling at each other, having decided to start over, or, more realistically, move forward after all the drama that has transpired.
